newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota says does not intend to curb exports to US.
newsitem.headline: Toyota says does not intend to curb exports to US.

text.p: Japan's top carmaker Toyota Motor Corp said on Friday that it had no intention of curbing its car exports to the United States.
Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda told a news conference in the western city of Nagoya that its car exports to the United States would grow by five percent this calendar year from the previous year.

Asked whether Toyota is trying to curb its exports to the U.S. in face of concerns over recurring trade friction, Okuda said: "We are not making such efforts. We've set up (our export) plans based on our supply and demand outlook and our U.S. exports this year will be up five percent year-on-year."
In calendar 1996, Toyota's exports to the U.S. stood at around 433,000 units.
Okuda also said Toyota was eager to attain a 40 percent domestic market share in sales. Toyota's domestic share in the first six months of this year stood at 38.8 percent.
Its domestic market share fell to 39.7 percent in 1996 from 40 percent the year before. It was the first time the top carmaker's share fell short of 40 percent in 14 years.

Okuda said that raising Toyota's stake in group telecom companies was one possible option the company could take in the future, but added that that he could not give any details now because a scheme on possible business alliances in the field had not yet been completed.
Okuda said that the company wants to make a decision on its plan to build a second car plant in Europe by the end of the year or early next year. He did not elaborate.
As for a joint venture with India's Kirloskar group, Toyota hopes to announce details later this year, Okuda said, without giving further details.
